summary: Instagram is doing nearly all the work: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube gives almost nothing (often under 30 views). The best videos are short, punchy Hindi pieces about a robot or sensor behaving in a surprising way, with a bold claim in the title. Generic 'how does X work?' videos about everyday devices (taps, doors, smoke alarms) get weak views, few likes and almost no saves or shares.
winningPattern: Robot or maker-project subject (gyro robot, clap switch, line follower, PIR, IR obstacle robot, mic) + a surprising 'it cannot do X, yet it does' hook in casual Hinglish + a short title ending with an emoji and #shorts, posted mainly for Instagram Reels. Titles that make a claim ('Taali Nahi, Sirf Shor Sunta Hai', 'Dimaag Nahi Hota', 'Bina Gyro Gir Jaata') beat neutral questions ('Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?'). Maker-relevant modules that viewers can build themselves earn the most likes, saves and shares.
doMore: Make robot and Arduino-module videos (gyro, clap switch, line follower, IR, mic) that students can copy, since these get the most views, likes and saves
Open with a bold or counter-intuitive claim in the title and first line instead of 'Kaise kaam karta hai?'
Show a visible before/after or fail/success moment (robot falls without gyro, light turns on with a clap) in the first 2 seconds
Add a save-worthy ending such as 'Save karo, build karte waqt kaam aayega' and a clear share prompt to boost saves and shares
Treat Instagram as the main platform and test YouTube separately with a different title, thumbnail frame or posting time before putting more effort there
stopDoing: Stop making generic everyday-device explainers (washroom tap, mall door, lift door, street light, smoke detector) with no build angle
Stop posting near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector videos, two automatic tap videos, two IR sensor videos) within days of each other
Stop expecting the same title and format to work on YouTube and Instagram without any changes
